methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Tandem PV is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised approximately $87 million to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 9 peer companies in the Climate & Energy sector, comprising 1 public company (Lanza Technologies, ticker LNZA) and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The peer-median method was not applicable in this case. The target company's narrow peer set—filtered by stage, valuation tier, and technology similarity—yielded fewer than the three datapoints required for reliable median triangulation. While nine same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the combined constraints of matching Series A stage, comparable funding tier, or sufficiently adjacent technology positioning. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial category error given the heterogeneity of climate tech subsectors and their distinct funding dynamics.

The absence of statistically robust comparable company analysis leaves this valuation assessment constrained. Without sufficient narrowly-filtered peers or disclosed financial metrics from the broader comp set, a quantified valuation range cannot be supported by the available data. Future valuation work on Tandem PV would benefit from either: (1) disclosure of revenue, capital intensity, or unit economics across the peer set, enabling revenue or cost-of-capital multiples, or (2) expansion of the peer universe to include adjacent-stage or adjacent-sector companies with defensible similarity claims. The key uncertainty remains the absence of standardized metrics suitable for triangulation.
